requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is enabled and active on node1.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was enabled and active before the restart, with matching runtime and permanent policy. After an acknowledged reboot and changed boot identity, firewalld recovered enabled and active with the same policy.
The installed rules explicitly accepted TCP/22, and isolated inbound SSH probes succeeded both before and after reboot.
TCP/8080 appeared in both runtime and permanent policy, the installed nftables rule accepted it, and probes reached a live TCP/8080 listener before and after reboot.

The public zone had a terminal REJECT target and catch-all nftables rejection. TCP/8081 was rejected despite a live listener, both before and after reboot, while unrelated pre-existing services were removed from the allowlist.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a persistent firewalld policy allowing SSH and TCP/8080 and rejecting other inbound traffic. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities; service, policy, packet behavior, and cleanup all recovered after reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The retained firewall change directly implemented the contract (cmd-712828e60c454cbb). Temporary namespaces, veth devices, listeners, and runtime interface assignments were necessary bounded probes and were fully removed (cmd-cc7bc38a9fd84039, cmd-16bce973f9774cac). The reboot was required by the provider restart protocol (cmd-313c6aa8f6de46ac). Final observations showed probe cleanup, no failed services, healthy package state, no unexpected listeners, and no executor-created temporary residue.
